title: QUIC Interop Runner HTTP/3 Endpoint Adapter Architecture
purpose: Define the harness-only adapter boundary for the QUIC interop-runner `http3` cell without moving HTTP/3 or QPACK protocol ownership into the transport core.
design_summary: The endpoint image remains the existing interop harness image and entrypoint. `TESTCASE=http3` is routed through a dedicated dispatch path that configures ALPN `h3`, opens the required HTTP/3 control and QPACK unidirectional streams through the HTTP/3 module, maps server request paths to files under `/www`, writes client downloads under `/downloads`, and preserves the runner exit-code contract. Existing non-HTTP/3 cells continue to use their current dispatch paths and ALPN. The HTTP/3 client/server wrappers attach to already-created managed QUIC connections/listeners so qlog, SSL key logging, deterministic local handshake keys, certificate loading, and endpoint-host behavior remain owned by the harness and transport seams already used by other interop cells.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The server endpoint binds UDP port 443 and uses `/certs/cert.pem` plus `/certs/priv.key` from the runner mount.
The client must treat every whitespace-separated `REQUESTS` URL as a download target and write each body to the matching path under `/downloads`.
The HTTP/3 runner cell must use ALPN `h3`; existing `hq-interop` dispatch paths must remain unchanged.
The adapter can use the current static/literal QPACK behavior and does not require dynamic QPACK usage for this slice.
Unsupported test cases must continue to return exit code 127.
The CI job is advisory local-runner evidence, not a broad peer matrix or upstream registry participation claim.
risks: The current HTTP/3 and QPACK modules are young; a green local runner cell must not be marketed as complete RFC 9114 or RFC 9204 coverage.
Running the upstream interop runner in CI depends on Docker and the external runner checkout, so CI should preserve artifacts and remain scoped to the `http3` cell.
